author: Temminck, 1836
summary: 우리나라에서는 남해의 섬에 나타나는 나그네새이자 겨울철새로, 해마다 수십 마리가 찾아온다. 아고산대 산지의 조릿대 숲에 살며, 여름에는 암수가 함께 지내면서 일정한 세력권을 지킨다. 주로 화본과와 꿀풀과 식물의 씨를 먹고 곤충도 잡아먹는다. 구북구 동부와 캄차카 등 아한대 지역에서 번식하며 한배에 알 5개를 낳고, 혼슈 중부와 류큐 등지에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Grey Bunting (Emberiza variabilis), adult male in winter, as seen on southern Korean islands: almost uniform dark slate-grey, the head and upperparts with faint olive-brown feather tips in fresh plumage; mantle and scapulars slate-grey with bold black shaft streaks and olive-buff edges; sides of the head and underparts slightly paler slate-grey, palest on the lower belly, without any yellow, streaking or white; wing coverts and flight feathers blackish-brown with greyish edges; rump plain grey; tail dark grey-brown with no white in the outer feathers; bill dark grey above, pinkish below; dark eye; pinkish legs.
art.pose: perched low in dense dwarf bamboo, side view
art.scene: southern Korean island: dense dwarf bamboo undergrowth on a wooded slope; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male winter, side view perched low in dwarf bamboo: slate-grey head and body, slightly paler grey below, black-streaked back with olive-buff fringes, blackish-brown wings, dark tail without white

adult male winter, back view perched: slate-grey mantle with bold black shaft streaks and olive-buff feather edges, blackish-brown wing coverts and flight feathers, plain grey rump, dark tail without white
art.build: Fairly large, long-tailed bunting, noticeably bigger and longer than a sparrow, with a rounded head and no crest. Bill conical, stout-based and pointed, about half the length of the head. Legs medium length, pinkish. At rest the wingtips reach only the base of the tail. Tail fairly long, slightly notched, uniformly dark with no white outer feathers, a key difference from most buntings. Skulks low in dense dwarf bamboo and on the ground beneath it.
avoid: Do not paint white outer tail feathers; the Grey Bunting's tail has no white.
Do not paint a yellowish belly, olive head or black face; those mark the male Black-faced Bunting (Emberiza spodocephala).
Do not paint a crest; the head is round.
Do not paint a white crown stripe or streaked underparts on the male.
